_meta.description: Griha Vastu Rules Database. To add or modify rules, edit this file only. The engine (vastu-engine.js) reads this at runtime and requires no code changes.
sources: Manasara (c. 5th century CE) — P.K. Acharya translation
Mayamata (c. 8th century CE) — Bruno Dagens translation
Samarangana Sutradhara (11th century CE) — King Bhoja of Dhar
IIT Kharagpur research on climatic basis of Vastu principles
Bureau of Indian Standards — National Building Code 2016

severity_levels.must_follow: Core Vastu principle — non-compliance significantly affects design score
severity_levels.recommended: Strongly advised — non-compliance reduces score moderately
severity_levels.good_to_have: Optional enhancement — included in full compliance reports
severity_levels.info: Contextual information — does not affect score

rules.title: Master bedroom in SW zone
rules.user_explanation: The SW zone (Nairutya) is governed by the earth element, providing stability and grounding — ideal for the head of household's bedroom.
rules.science_bridge: SW rooms in India typically receive afternoon sun, maintaining warmth into the evening which promotes better sleep onset.

rules.title: Bed head direction — south or east preferred
rules.user_explanation: Sleeping with your head pointing south or east aligns with Earth's magnetic field. Sleeping with head pointing north creates opposing polarity and can disturb sleep.
rules.science_bridge: Research from the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS) suggests geomagnetic alignment may influence sleep quality.

rules.title: No mirror directly facing the bed
rules.user_explanation: Mirrors facing the bed are said to reflect energy back during sleep, causing restlessness and disturbed dreams. Place mirrors on the north wall or inside wardrobe doors.
rules.science_bridge: From a psychological standpoint, seeing one's reflection when waking at night can cause brief disorientation, affecting sleep quality.

rules.title: Overhead structural beam above sleeping area
rules.user_explanation: A structural beam directly above the sleeping position creates oppressive energy. Solutions: canopy bed, fabric drape across beam, or a false ceiling below the beam.
rules.science_bridge: Studies in environmental psychology show that low visual 'weight' overhead (perceived ceiling compression) can increase reported stress levels during sleep.

rules.title: Kitchen in SE zone (Agni corner)
rules.user_explanation: The SE zone is ruled by Agni (fire) — the ideal placement for all cooking spaces. A kitchen in the NE zone is considered particularly inauspicious in Vastu.
rules.science_bridge: SE-facing kitchens in India receive morning and early-afternoon sunlight, maximising natural ventilation and reducing humidity — a practical health benefit.

rules.title: Cook should face east while cooking
rules.user_explanation: Positioning the hob/stove so the cook faces east (towards the rising sun) while cooking is considered auspicious and energising.
rules.science_bridge: East-facing cooking positions receive morning light without glare, reducing eye strain during meal preparation.

rules.title: Living room in north or east zones
rules.user_explanation: The living/drawing room should occupy the NE, N, E, or NW zones. These directions receive morning light and support positive social interaction.
rules.science_bridge: North and east-facing rooms in India receive consistent indirect light throughout the day — better for social activities and reducing eye fatigue.

rules.title: Heavy furniture along south or west walls
rules.user_explanation: Sofas and heavy furniture should be placed along the south or west walls. This grounds the heavier elements and keeps the north-east zone open and light.
rules.science_bridge: Placing bulk furniture against south/west walls naturally creates a focal point facing east/north — towards the better-lit portion of the room.

rules.title: Washroom in NW, W, or S zones
rules.user_explanation: Bathrooms should occupy the NW, W, or S zones. Never in the NE — this is the sacred Ishanya zone and must remain pure.
rules.science_bridge: NW placement ensures drainage flows away from the living areas and the prevailing south-west winds carry odours away from the main habitable spaces.

rules.title: Pooja room in NE zone (Ishanya)
rules.user_explanation: The NE zone is the most sacred direction, governed by divine cosmic energy. The pooja room or mandir must occupy this zone for maximum positive energy.
rules.science_bridge: NE rooms in India receive the early morning sun — the most beneficial light quality. The gentle morning light creates a naturally calming atmosphere ideal for prayer.

rules.title: Balcony in north or east preferred
rules.user_explanation: Balconies on the north or east side receive morning light and breezes. South and SW balconies receive harsh afternoon sun.
rules.science_bridge: East-facing balconies receive sun only in the morning, keeping them naturally cooler and more usable through the day — particularly important in Indian climate.

rules.title: Main entrance — north, east, or NE facing
rules.user_explanation: The main entrance should ideally face north, east, or northeast. These directions welcome positive energy and morning light into the home.
rules.science_bridge: North and east-facing entrances keep the interior cooler in the mornings and reduce direct western sun exposure — practical in Indian climate.

rules.title: Keep the NE zone light and uncluttered
rules.user_explanation: The NE corner of every room and the home overall should be kept light, open, and clutter-free. Never place heavy furniture or storage in the NE.
rules.science_bridge: Keeping the NE corner (which receives morning light) open ensures maximum natural light penetration and air circulation into the living spaces.

rules.title: Warm earth tones for SW master bedroom
rules.user_explanation: The SW zone's earth element is complemented by warm earthy tones — terracotta, beige, warm browns, deep cream. Avoid harsh reds or black.
rules.science_bridge: Warm earth tones have been shown in colour psychology (NCS research) to promote feelings of security and restfulness — ideal for a bedroom.

rules.title: Warm tones (orange, yellow) for SE kitchen
rules.user_explanation: The SE fire zone is energised by warm colours. Orange and yellow support the Agni energy. Avoid green and blue — water element colours that conflict with fire.
rules.science_bridge: Orange and yellow hues are associated with appetite stimulation and energetic activity in colour psychology research — both beneficial in a kitchen context.

rules.title: Light greens and blues for north-facing living rooms
rules.user_explanation: North and NE living rooms are enhanced by green, blue, and white tones which align with the water and air elements governing these zones.
rules.science_bridge: Cool tones in well-lit north-facing rooms avoid visual overheating and create a balanced luminous environment without glare.
